"""Bulk user import from an uploaded CSV.

Implement import_users.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class ImportResult:
    """PROVIDED. Do not change the field names -- the admin UI renders them."""

    users: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


REQUIRED_COLUMNS = ("email", "name", "team")


def import_users(csv_text: str) -> ImportResult:
    """Parse an uploaded CSV into user records.

    Contract (fixed -- the admin upload view calls it this way):

        result = import_users(csv_text)
        result.users   -> list of dicts, one per data row, keyed by the header column names
        result.errors  -> human-readable problems, one string each

    The first line is the header and names the columns. `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` must all be
    present; anything else in the header is carried through as-is.

    A row that cannot be imported goes in `errors` and is left out of `users`. A file with
    unimportable rows still imports the rows that are fine.
    """
    result = ImportResult()
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(csv_text))

    try:
        header = next(reader)
    except StopIteration:
        result.errors.append("File is empty.")
        return result

    # Customer exports vary -- strip stray whitespace and a leading BOM on the first column.
    header = [column.strip().lstrip("﻿") for column in header]

    missing_columns = [c for c in REQUIRED_COLUMNS if c not in header]
    if missing_columns:
        result.errors.append(
            f"Missing required column(s): {', '.join(missing_columns)}"
        )
        return result

    for line_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
        if not row or all(cell.strip() == "" for cell in row):
            continue

        if len(row) != len(header):
            result.errors.append(
                f"Row {line_number}: expected {len(header)} columns, got {len(row)}"
            )
            continue

        record = dict(zip(header, row))

        blank_fields = [c for c in REQUIRED_COLUMNS if not record[c].strip()]
        if blank_fields:
            result.errors.append(
                f"Row {line_number}: missing value(s) for {', '.join(blank_fields)}"
            )
            continue

        result.users.append(record)

    return result

"""The tests that shipped with the ticket."""
from app.importer import import_users


def test_imports_a_simple_file():
    result = import_users(
        "email,name,team\n"
        "ada@example.com,Ada Lovelace,Engineering\n"
        "grace@example.com,Grace Hopper,Engineering\n"
    )
    assert result.errors == []
    assert len(result.users) == 2
    assert result.users[0]["email"] == "ada@example.com"
    assert result.users[1]["name"] == "Grace Hopper"


def test_missing_required_column_is_an_error():
    result = import_users("email,name\nada@example.com,Ada Lovelace\n")
    assert result.errors
    assert result.users == []


def test_extra_columns_are_kept():
    result = import_users(
        "email,name,team,title\nada@example.com,Ada Lovelace,Engineering,Analyst\n"
    )
    assert result.errors == []
    assert result.users[0]["title"] == "Analyst"

from app.importer import import_users

# duplicate header columns
r = import_users("email,name,team,team\nada@example.com,Ada,Eng,Sales\n")
print("dup header:", r.users, r.errors)

# case-varied header (common Excel export)
r = import_users("Email,Name,Team\nada@example.com,Ada,Eng\n")
print("case header:", r.users, r.errors)

# duplicate email rows
r = import_users("email,name,team\nada@example.com,Ada,Eng\nada@example.com,Ada2,Sales\n")
print("dup email:", r.users, r.errors)

# malformed email accepted
r = import_users("email,name,team\nnot-an-email,Ada,Eng\n")
print("bad email:", r.users, r.errors)

# formula-injection-style field
r = import_users('email,name,team\n=CMD(\"calc\"),Ada,Eng\n')
print("formula:", r.users, r.errors)
EOF

content.text: Confirmed the failure modes empirically. Here are the findings.

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "case-sensitive-header-match",
      "title": "Header column matching is case-sensitive, so common Excel/HR export headers reject the whole file",
      "requirement": "The ticket states files come from 'the customer's own systems — HR exports, spreadsheets, whatever they've got' and the code itself acknowledges header variance by stripping whitespace/BOM; a competent import must tolerate the header-casing variance (`Email`/`EMAIL` vs `email`) that Excel and HR tools routinely produce.",
      "evidence": "app/importer.py:50 does `c not in header` with no case-folding. A file with `Email,Name,Team` as the header is verified to produce `Missing required column(s): email, name, team` and zero imported users, even though every required field is present.",
      "failure": "An admin uploads a perfectly good 340-row customer export whose header happens to be capitalized (very common from Excel/Workday/BambooHR exports) and the entire import is rejected with a confusing 'missing column' error, forcing the admin to manually edit the file before every upload.",
      "severity": "high"
    },
    {
      "id": "duplicate-header-silently-drops-data",
      "title": "Duplicate column names in the header silently overwrite data instead of being reported as an error",
      "requirement": "The contract requires 'A row that cannot be imported goes in errors' — a malformed/ambiguous header (two columns with the same name) makes every row's mapping for that column ambiguous and undetectable, which is a file-level defect that must be reported, not silently resolved by last-write-wins.",
      "evidence": "app/importer.py:67 does `record = dict(zip(header, row))`. Verified: header `email,name,team,team` with row `ada@example.com,Ada,Eng,Sales` produces `{'team': 'Sales'}` — the 'Eng' value is silently discarded with no error and no indication to the admin that data was lost.",
      "failure": "A customer HR export with a repeated or badly-generated header column (common when exports are hand-edited or merged from multiple systems) causes real field values to vanish without any error message, and the admin has no way to know a user's team/data was dropped.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "no-duplicate-email-detection",
      "title": "Duplicate emails within the same file are imported as two separate, conflicting user records with no error",
      "requirement": "Email is the natural unique identity key for a user account; a bulk-provisioning import must treat a second row with the same email as an import conflict to report back to the admin, per the same 'rows that can't be imported get reported' contract — this is exactly the kind of dirty data the ticket says these uncontrolled customer exports will contain.",
      "evidence": "app/importer.py has no dedup/uniqueness check across rows. Verified: two rows with `ada@example.com` (different name/team) both land in `result.users` with `errors == []`.",
      "failure": "Downstream user creation either throws an unhandled unique-constraint error for the whole batch, or silently creates/overwrites the user with whichever row processes last — the admin gets no warning that the source file had a conflicting duplicate, and account data (team assignment) may end up wrong with no audit trail.",
      "severity": "high"
    },
    {
      "id": "no-email-syntax-validation",
      "title": "The email column is only checked for non-blank, not for valid email syntax",
      "requirement": "A user-provisioning pipeline consuming an 'email' field must validate it is a syntactically plausible address (RFC 5321/5322 shape) before treating it as an identity/contact channel; the ticket explicitly flags these files as coming from uncontrolled customer systems, i.e. dirty-data is the expected case this feature must guard against.",
      "evidence": "app/importer.py:69 only checks `not record[c].strip()` for required columns. Verified: a row with email value `not-an-email` is accepted into `result.users` with no error.",
      "failure": "Garbage or truncated email values from a bad HR export (e.g. a name accidentally shifted into the email column) get provisioned as real accounts; invites/notifications later silently fail to deliver, and the admin only discovers it when users report never receiving onboarding email — well after the import appeared to succeed.",
      "severity": "medium"
    }
  ]
}
```
